results.title: Partial order that is a union of countably many antichains
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A partial order (P, ≤) is a *union of ω antichains* if P = ⋃_{n<ω} Aₙ where each Aₙ ⊆ P is an antichain (a set of pairwise ≤-incomparable elements).

results.title: Special partial order
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A partial order (α,≤) is *special* if there is a map f : α → ℚ that is strictly increasing, i.e.\ x < y implies f(x) < f(y). Note that f need not be injective: nothing is required of incomparable elements.

results.title: Rough numbers
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $n$ and $k$ be natural numbers. Then $n$ is $k$-rough if $n \neq 0$ and every prime $p$ dividing $n$ satisfies $k < p$; that is, $n$ is positive and has no prime factor at most $k$.

results.title: Rough numbers are positive

results.title: Roughness through the list of prime factors
results.caption: Theorem

results.title: Boolean functions increasing in a variable

results.title: Non-degenerate Boolean functions

results.title: Threshold language of a counting function
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a function $f$ from bitstrings to natural numbers, the threshold language of $f$ is the decision problem that accepts a bitstring $y$ exactly when decoding $y$ with the canonical bitstring encoding of pairs of a bitstring and a natural number succeeds and gives a pair $(x, k)$ with $k \le f(x)$; bitstrings that do not decode are rejected.

results.title: Threshold languages of #P functions are in PSPACE

results.title: The depth interpretation
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a signature $\sigma$, the depth interpretation is the interpretation of $\sigma$ in $\mathbb{N}$ that sends an operation symbol of arity $k$, applied to argument depths $d_0, \dots, d_{k-1}$, to $\max(0, d_0, \dots, d_{k-1}) + 1$: a gate is one deeper than its deepest argument, and a gate without arguments has depth $1$.

results.title: Gate depths are evaluation in the depth interpretation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every program $p$ over a signature $\sigma$, the depth of each gate of $p$ equals the value of that gate when $p$ is evaluated under the depth interpretation of $\sigma$ with every input set to $0$.

results.title: Depth of an arithmetic gate
results.caption: Theorem

results.title: Depth of the carry gates
results.caption: Theorem

results.title: ARACNE gene network reconstruction
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The network ARACNE reconstructs from symmetric pairwise mutual informations `I` with independence threshold `I₀` and DPI tolerance zero (Margolin et al. 2006): `{i, k}` is an edge iff `i ≠ k`, `I₀ < I i k`, and no third gene `j` with `I₀ < I i j` and `I₀ < I j k` has `I i k < min (I i j) (I j k)`.

results.title: No false negatives
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If the true network `T` is a forest whose edges all carry mutual information above `I₀`, and `I a b ≤ min (I a c) (I c b)` whenever `c` separates `a` from `b` in `T` (every walk from `a` to `b` visits `c`), then ARACNE keeps every edge of `T`.

results.title: No false positives
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If the true network `T` is a tree and `I a b < min (I a c) (I c b)` whenever `c` separates `a` from `b` in `T`, then every edge ARACNE keeps is an edge of `T`.

results.title: ARACNE recovers tree networks exactly
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: ARACNE recovers tree networks exactly (Margolin et al. 2006, Theorem 1): if the true network `T` is a tree whose edges all carry mutual information above `I₀`, and the strict data-processing inequality holds on every separated triple, then ARACNE returns `T`. Strictness is the explicit form of the paper's exclusion of exact cancellations; with equality ARACNE can keep an indirect edge (see the tests).

results.title: Chow–Liu trees survive ARACNE
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Chow–Liu trees survive ARACNE (Margolin et al. 2006, Theorem 2): a spanning tree `T` of maximum total weight `∑_{{i, k} ∈ T} I i k` among all spanning trees, whose edges all carry mutual information above `I₀`, is a subnetwork of the ARACNE network.

results.title: Derivative of the binomial upper tail
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Derivative of the binomial upper tail in the success probability: for `1 ≤ k ≤ n`, `d/dp P(Bin(n, p) ≥ k) = n C(n - 1, k - 1) p^(k-1) (1-p)^(n-k)` at every real `p` (the sum telescopes).

results.title: The binomial upper tail is nondecreasing in `p` on `(0, 1)`
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The binomial upper tail is nondecreasing in `p` on `[0, 1]`, for every `n` and `k`.

results.title: The binomial upper tail is strictly increasing in `p` on `(0, 1)`
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The binomial upper tail is strictly increasing in `p` on `[0, 1]` when `1 ≤ k ≤ n`.

results.title: Binomial z-score approximation to the motif conservation score
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The conserved count `k` of a motif with `N` occurrences, standardized under `Bin(N, p)`: `(k - N p) / √(N p (1 - p))`. This is an approximation to Xie et al.'s MCS, not their exact score.

results.title: Motif conservation score approximation is strictly increasing
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The MCS approximation is strictly increasing in the conserved count, for `N ≥ 1` and `p ∈ (0, 1)`.

results.title: Motif conservation score approximation as a de Moivre–Laplace sum
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The MCS approximation of the number of conserved occurrences among the first `n` is the de Moivre–Laplace standardized sum.

results.title: De Moivre–Laplace for the MCS approximation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If the conservation indicators of the occurrences are i.i.d. Bernoulli(`p`) with `0 < p < 1`, then for every `z`, `P(z ≤ MCS approximation of the first n occurrences)` tends to the standard normal mass of `[z, ∞)`.

results.title: The SiPhy rate matrix
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The SiPhy rate matrix `Q a b = ω R a b π b` for `a ≠ b` (Garber et al. 2009, Eq. 10), with rows summing to zero: `ω` times the GTR matrix with exchangeabilities `R` and base frequencies `π`.

results.title: SiPhy matrix is a rate matrix
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: With `ω ≥ 0`, nonnegative `R` and nonnegative `π`, the SiPhy matrix is a rate matrix.

results.title: `π` is the equilibrium of the SiPhy matrix
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For symmetric `R` it is in detailed balance with `π`, for every `ω`.

results.title: The expected complete-data log-likelihood
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The expected complete-data log-likelihood of a rate matrix `Q` and root distribution `π` (Garber et al. 2009, Eq. 6): `∑_{a ≠ b} n a b log Q a b + ∑ a, τ a Q a a + ∑ b, r b log π b`, for expected substitution counts `n`, expected state durations `τ` and the root posterior `r`.

results.title: Expected total number of substitutions
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The expected total number of substitutions `N = ∑_{a ≠ b} n a b`.

results.title: Weight of a state: substitutions into it plus root posterior
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The weight `c b = ∑_{a ≠ b} n a b + r b` of state `b`: substitutions into `b` plus the root posterior of `b`.

results.title: Time-weighted exchange rate into a state
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The time-weighted exchange rate into `b`, `e b = ∑_{a ≠ b} τ a R a b`.

results.title: Part of the SiPhy objective depending on the constraint vector
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The part of Eq. 6 that depends on `π` (for fixed `ω`): `∑ b, (c b * log (π b) - d b * π b)`.

results.title: Constant $n \log R$ term of the SiPhy objective
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The `n log R` constant of Eq. 6.

results.title: Eq. 6 for the SiPhy matrix
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For `ω > 0`, positive off-diagonal `R` and positive `π`, `expectedLogLik = N log ω + ∑_{a ≠ b} n a b log R a b + piObjective c (ω e) π`.

results.title: The SiPhy rate update
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The SiPhy rate update (Eq. 7, for fixed `π`): `ω = N / ∑ b, e b π b`.

results.title: The rate update maximizes Eq. 6 over `ω > 0`
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The rate update maximizes Eq. 6 over `ω > 0` for a fixed positive `π`, when the expected number of substitutions `N` and the time-weighted rate `∑ b, e b π b` are positive.

results.title: The rate update is the unique maximizer
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Any other `ω > 0` gives a strictly smaller value of Eq. 6.

results.title: The Lagrange multiplier of the `π` update exists and is unique
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For positive `c` and nonnegative `d` on a nonempty finite alphabet there is exactly one `γ` with `d b + γ > 0` for all `b` and `∑ b, c b / (d b + γ) = 1`.

results.title: The `π` update is the unique maximizer
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The `π` update is the unique maximizer of `piObjective c d` over the positive probability vectors: with `γ` as in `existsUnique_lagrange`, every other positive `π` summing to one has a strictly smaller objective than `b ↦ c b / (d b + γ)`.

results.title: The SiPhy constraint-vector update
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The SiPhy constraint-vector update (Eq. 8, for fixed `ω`): `π b = c b / (ω e b + γ)`, with `γ` the Lagrange multiplier of `existsUnique_lagrange`.

results.title: The constraint-vector update is the unique maximizer of Eq. 6
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The constraint-vector update is the unique maximizer of Eq. 6 over the positive probability vectors `π` (the rate matrix `ω R π` and the root distribution both use `π`), for fixed `ω > 0`, positive off-diagonal `R` and positive weights `c`.

results.title: Leaf set meeting both sides of a tree edge
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Whether the leaf set `S` meets both sides of an edge with leaf set `B` below it, inside a tree with leaf set `U`: `S ∩ B` and `S ∩ (U \ B)` are nonempty.

results.title: Nonnegative edge lengths of a tree
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Edge lengths are nonnegative: every dart's undirected edge has nonnegative length.

results.title: Total branch length of a tree
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The total branch length: half the sum of the edge lengths over the darts, since each undirected edge is traversed once in each direction.

results.title: The Branch Length Score
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The Branch Length Score (unnormalized): the total branch length of the smallest subtree of `T` connecting the leaves `S`, as half the sum over the darts of the edge length times the indicator that `S` meets both sides (`edgeSide`) of the dart's edge.

results.title: Normalized branch length score
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The normalized Branch Length Score, `bls S T w / totalLength T w`, as reported by Kheradpour et al. (a fraction of the total branch length).

results.title: Branch length score is nonnegative for nonnegative edge lengths
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The BLS is nonnegative for nonnegative edge lengths.

results.title: Branch length score is at most the tree length for nonnegative lengths
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The BLS is at most the total branch length.

results.title: Monotonicity
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: With nonnegative edge lengths, more conserving species never lower the BLS.

results.title: Branch length score of the empty set is zero
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The BLS of the empty set is `0`.

results.title: A single species has BLS `0`
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A single species has BLS `0` (a motif present in one genome is not conserved).

results.title: All species give the whole tree
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The BLS of the set of all leaves is the total branch length.

results.title: Subadditivity
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For sets of species `S`, `S'` that share a species, the subtree connecting `S ∪ S'` is at most as long as the two subtrees together.

results.title: Normalized branch length score is nonnegative for nonnegative lengths
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The normalized BLS is nonnegative.

results.title: Normalized branch length score is at most one for nonnegative lengths
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The normalized BLS is at most `1` when the tree has positive total length.

results.title: The side of a pendant edge is the singleton of its leaf
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The taxa whose leaf is closer to the leaf vertex than to its neighbor are exactly that leaf's taxon.

results.title: Sum over darts is twice the sum over edges
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A sum over darts of a function of the undirected edge is twice the sum over the edges: the two darts of each edge contribute equally.
